title: Reuse imported evaluations and native completion proofs without transferring live authority
outcome: Matching imported evaluations and foreign native completion seals support local acceptance/child completion accounting through explicit provenance-preserving references, without fabricating local completed runs or transferring claims.
acceptance: Imported evaluation reuse compares the retained governing content fingerprint with an exact independently identified snapshot, actual destination criteria/bindings/policy/mode/source and eligible cited evidence. Tests distinguish fingerprints from object links, equal versus changed governing content, unavailable exact snapshots, evaluator independence and superseded verdicts; import alone creates no verdict or model rerun.

Foreign native completion seals retain their integer accepted_work_revision and minted accepted_work_revision_hash object link, original cuts, required children, waivers, environment and evidence closure. A new local completion/parent seal may reference an applicable foreign native proof explicitly under existing rules; it never installs that seal as a local run completion or treats reported/restored prose as native proof.

Behavioral tests exercise valid foreign child/completion proof reuse, mismatched governing/source/feed context, incomplete closure, reopened/new local generations, and inert reported completion. Original ids/bytes/links/seals stay fixed, local claims/report assembly/session delivery never transfer, and later findings do not rewrite frozen historical decisions.

Reuse is integrated with accepted family outcomes and current verification eligibility, including conflicting terminal evidence and missing optional artifact bytes where a criterion actually needs them. Exact repeat/reverse import is stable and atomic failure leaves no local partial acceptance/seal. Unsupported acceptance-string mapping remains explicit; this slice does not silently activate evaluations or add a new gate.
